rationale: This historical econometric study (244 cities across four Prussian provinces, 1880-1887) tests how local municipal governance and electoral-fiscal institutions—specifically Prussia's tax-weighted Three Class System of town council representation versus equal-vote restricted municipal franchises, interacted with local tax skew—shaped municipal decisions to construct community waterworks networks. Financing, tariff, and special frontage assessment rules (fees_tariffs_subsidies) and cross-national worker wage burdens (economic_access) are examined descriptively to motivate the net-benefit incidence framework, while the primary empirical model is an observational cross-sectional logit analysis (with an instrumental variable for capacity cost) predicting municipal waterworks adoption/network provision (primary_connection).
